messages:
emma: Quick sync — onboarding modal rolled out yesterday. Seeing 3 reproducing bugs and ~8 small UX asks from early customers. Need to decide what we patch in a 2-week post-launch fix vs what goes into the next-wave enhancements. Priorities?
noah: Main bug is the modal submitting duplicate requests when users double-click next. Causes double invoice lines for some customers. Repro in prod for 3 orgs, high priority. :bug:
sam: I can put a hotfix branch for the double-submit check. Minimal change: debounce + idempotency token. Should be safe for a fast patch.
ria: UX asks are mostly micro: confirmation copy, button spacing, and a suggestive tooltip for pricing tiers. None are blocking flows but improve conversion.
marta: Metrics: onboarding funnel drop increased by 2.4% yesterday, but the double-invoice cases are customer-visible (billing outliers) — highest severity from CS.
jules: Customer asks include a request to surface 'estimated monthly' on the modal (feature request) — would be a medium-term enhancement.
emma: Proposal: 1) Urgent patch for double-submit (1.5-day work + QA), 2) small UX polish batch for week 2 if bandwidth, 3) larger features (estimated monthly) to next milestone. Agree?
sam: +1 to hotfix. I'll open a PR today and flag eng-oncall for a canary deploy.
noah: CS asks we priority-fix billing-visible issues first, customers are sensitive. Will prepare comms for affected customers.
ria: For polish batch, will create a micro-epic with 3 screens and expected copy changes. Low engineering cost but needs design review.
marta: Can we gate the polish on conversion lift threshold? If we don't see >1% improvement after hotfix, we deprioritize polish to next cycle.
emma: Good call. Let's set a 7-day measurement window post-hotfix. If conversion improves >=1% we ship the polish in sprint 2; otherwise move to backlog.
jules: I'll add the 'estimated monthly' ask to the public roadmap with a note: "customer-suggested, requires product validation".
sam: Quick tech note for the hotfix: using idempotency-token header + client-side debounce. Example middleware I plan to add:
```
function idempotency(req, res, next) {
  const id = req.headers['x-idempotency-key'];
  if (!id) return next();
  if (cache.has(id)) return res.status(409).send('duplicate');
  cache.set(id, true, { ttl: 60 * 60 });
  next();
}
```
noah: Excellent. Also want an ops rollback plan: if billing spikes after the deploy, rollback and revert in <30m.
emma: Action items:
- sam: open hotfix PR and target canary deploy (due today)
- noah: draft customer comms for affected accounts (due EOD)
- ria: create polish micro-epic + copy changes (due tomorrow)
- marta: define conversion gating metric and dashboard (due EOD)
- jules: add roadmap note and link to ticket (due tomorrow)
We'll reconvene in 48h to decide sprint placement for polish. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
